Such documentation may include a properly executed lease or rental77 agreement or proof of rental payments.78 (3) If such person is unable to provide the documentation required by paragraph (2) of79 this subsection, such person shall be subject to arrest for unlawful squatting and upon80 conviction to the penalty provided in subsection (b) of this Code section.81 (4) If such person does provide documentation that authorizes such person's entry on the82 land or premises, a hearing shall be set within seven days of the submission of such83 documentation and if the court finds that the submitted documentation was not properly84 executed or is not meritorious, such person shall be subject to demand for possession and85 removal as provided in Code Section 44-11-32, be subject to arrest and upon conviction86 penalties as provided for in Code Sections 16-9-1 and 16-9-2, and shall be assessed an87 additional fine based on the fair market monthly rental rate of the land or premises.88 (b)(c) Any person who violates subsection (a) (b) of this Code section shall be guilty of89 a misdemeanor which and upon conviction thereof, shall be punishable punished as90 provided in Code Section 17-10-3 and, further, shall be ordered to make restitution to the91 property owner, rightful occupant of the property, or authorized representative of the92 property owner. others to immediately vacate, real property are the most important real183 property rights. The General Assembly further finds that existing remedies regarding a184 squatter, also known as an unauthorized person who unlawfully remains or resides on real185 property, fail to adequately protect the rights of the real property owner and fail to186 adequately discourage theft and vandalism. The intent of this Code section is to swiftly187 restore possession of real property to the lawful owner of the property when such property188 is being unlawfully occupied and to thereby preserve real property rights while limiting the189 opportunity for criminal activity.190 (c) A real property owner or his or her authorized agent may request from the sheriff,191 deputy sheriff, constable, marshal, or other peace officer certified by the Georgia Peace192 Officer Standards and Training Council of the county in which the real property is located193 the immediate removal of a person or persons unlawfully residing on or within the real194 property pursuant to this Code section, subject to the following conditions:195 (1) The requesting person is the real property owner or authorized agent of the real196 property owner;197 (2) An unauthorized person or persons have unlawfully entered and remain or continue198 to reside on or within the property owner's real property;199 (3) The real property was not open to members of the public at the time the unauthorized200 person or persons entered;201 (4) The real property owner has directed the unauthorized person or persons to leave the202 real property;203 (5) The unauthorized person or persons are not current tenants pursuant to a written or204 oral rental agreement authorized by the real property owner;205 (6) The unauthorized person or persons are not immediate family members of the real206 property owner;
